title: Ledoit-Wolf covariance shrinkage
purpose: Shrink a sample covariance toward a scaled identity with the Ledoit-Wolf intensity, giving a well-conditioned, positive definite estimate even when there are fewer observations than variables. Use it before inverting a covariance of metrics, features or embeddings estimated from few runs.

entry_points.name: ledoit_wolf
entry_points.arguments: rows: at least 2 observations of p variables; assume_centered: bool
entry_points.returns: {covariance, sample_covariance, shrinkage, target_scale, d_squared, b_bar_squared, smallest_eigenvalue, sample_smallest_eigenvalue}

entry_points.name: shrink
entry_points.arguments: covariance: symmetric p by p; shrinkage in [0, 1]

assumptions: Observations are independent and identically distributed with finite fourth moments (the setting of the consistency result).
The sample covariance divides by n, as in the Ledoit-Wolf derivation.
guarantees: shrinkage = min(bbar^2, d^2) / d^2 lies in [0, 1]; it is 0 when the sample covariance is already a multiple of the identity.
With shrinkage > 0 and a positive target scale the estimate is positive definite, even when p > n.
Scaling the data by c scales the estimate by c^2 and leaves the shrinkage unchanged; rotating the data rotates the estimate.

known_wrong.name: not_left_singular
known_wrong.why: With 3 observations of 5 variables the sample covariance is singular; using it unshrunk makes its inverse undefined.

limits: Single target (scaled identity); other targets such as constant correlation or a diagonal are not included. The intensity is an estimate of the loss-minimizing value with an asymptotic guarantee, not the oracle intensity for a given small sample. Dense p by p matrices: meant for p up to a few hundred.
technique_references: A well-conditioned estimator for large-dimensional covariance matrices (Ledoit and Wolf)
Linear shrinkage toward a scaled identity target
